questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The reason for choosing Utrecht University was the high level of education you receive at UU. They had an interesting European and International programme in Law, and UU have received lots of appreciation from former students.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It is an amazing experience, and I would encourage everybody to take the opportunity to study abroad. It is a learning experience, and you really get to know yourself better and improve your english skills.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was quite easy. UU has a great office that can respond on every question within short time. They are very warm, and you receive many information about the University.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I had many questions regarding the grading system, which is quite different in the Netherlands.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Student Housing is a possibility through 'SSH'. But be prepared; it is very, very hard to find accommodation in the Netherlands. There is not many apartment through SSH, and all apartments through SSH are being put up for grabs at the same time online, and from that on it is just first come first served.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: In the apartments through SSH you live with other international students. You have your own room, and then you share a kitchen with 2-4 other students. I lived with 3 other international students and we had two fridges.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: It is a great place. You have a store, library, pizza place and food trunks. It is 5km from the city center, but when you have a bike from swapfiets it does not take more than 15-20 minutes to get there. There is also bus and trams, which is available 24/7

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I had a great experience. Because of that I give the grade of 5. BUT I know about many international students who spent a long time finding accommodations, and it is very expensive to live in a hotel here in Utrecht. So be aware, and prioritise to find accommodations fast.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was fairly easy. If you were in doubt, just text them. They answer quite fast.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The process is easy to follow. You get much help from your own institution and the host institution. You need to provide some information, but nothing to be worried about.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You can easily get help through both your own institution and the host institution.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the courses I applied for.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Text them if you are in doubt. They are very helpful.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Very, very satisfied. They have a high level of education, and high level educators. Simply incredible.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level is high. But it is what you can expect from a course at MA level. You really have to keep up with the reading list, because there is a lot of reading and very little time to prepare.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: I would describe UU as an institution whose style of teaching is more on the theoretical level, where UCPH is focusing more practice. You have a short period to prepare for the exam, which is quite different from UCPH. Your grade is also not just associated with the final exam, but here at UU you have 2-3 "exams", where you have to hand in a paper or make an oral presentation. These may between 10-50% of your final grade.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Judicial Protection and Enforcement of EU Law
International Security Law
Constitutional Law of the European Union
International Humanitarian Law

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would definitely recommend all courses, but especially the courses of International Security Law and International Humanitarian Law. These are the best courses I have ever had. Great teachers, exiting discussions, great way of structuring the seminars.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There is a lot of possibilities.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I participated in the UU Welcome Week. Many students also joins other things, but I chose to focus on Uni.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: ESN, Buddy-go Dutch, UU Welcome.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: There is not far to anywhere in the Netherlands. You have to visit Amsterdam, Den Haag and Maastricht. Wonderful cities.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy. Dutch people are very good at english.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Be open-minded. The dutch student on the international programmes speak english nearly all the time. They are very friendly!

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Dutch people can be very direct. Be aware of that and don't take anything to personal :-)

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Their open-mindedness.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Be prepared for the time you have to spent on studying. It is more extensive down here. 
Read everything on time. The lectures and seminars are important to pass the exams. And prepared for many various 'exams.'
Spent time with the other international (or dutch) students. A social network is important in a new country.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Get a Swapfiets. Very cheap and biking is by far the easiest way of transport in Utrecht. 
Get a tripkey card, which you can travel on within netherlands. 
Be aware that not all stores take VISA cards. Albert Heijn, the biggest supermarket, do not use VISA. 
Remember your raincoat. It is raining a lot ;-)

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The level of education. What an amazing experience. UU have some of the best teachers. I have really enjoyed my courses.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: the greatest challenge has also been the most rewarding part. The level of education. You are expected to read a lot, and they keep you on your toes with assignments and oral presentations, so you don't just have a final exam.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Utrecht University, the place you have to go study.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
